anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps both facts: the round-1 edit adds only the `--check` literal to the `**Verification:**` header line with an explicit 'replacing and removing nothing' note and no task-body change, and the continuation runs `skip plan` with `resume: pasted brief`, `start implement`, and `plan_tracker init` with the brief's four tasks in the same names, order and statuses. Nothing in After moved either fact. Since this input is a task-plan (non-ledger) brief, retaining `init` is correct here; keep the no-init/one-refresh wording from the Change scoped to ledger-backed briefs so task-plan cases like this continue to show the unchanged four-task init. One minor tidy-up: the phrase 'matches the row `quote-integrity`, `Verification`-owned row' is garbled and could read 'matches the `quote-integrity` check on the `Verification`-owned citation row' without affecting any fact.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved between Before and After on this case. Both outputs add only the missing `--check` literal to the `**Verification:**` header line and leave every task body untouched (f1), and both continue with `phase_tracker skip plan`, `phase_tracker start implement`, and a `plan_tracker init` carrying the brief's four tasks with their statuses unchanged (f3). The After rewording tightens the citation-repair step (naming the prior git results as the tracked/clean evidence and requiring the anchor to resolve before the edit) and reformats the tracker calls as inline calls rather than a JSON blob, but these are presentational and preserve every fact.
